newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom push takes NZ shares to new record close.
newsitem.headline: Telecom push takes NZ shares to new record close.

text.p: A strong morning spurt in the final session of a week of record highs on the New Zealand stock exchange provoked a new scramble for shares in Telecom and squeezed the Top 40 index up to another record close.
Brokers said the pattern of trade, a solid early climb followed by a midday trough then a run-up at the end, left Telecom in central focus with some positions still short.
"I think there's probably a bit of pain being endured out there in Telecom," one senior dealer said.
Although the market retreated from an intraday high of 2,538 points, the index closed up nearly seven points at 2,526.65.
Volume of NZ$67.9 million was deceptive in that it did not reflect broad-based activity, dealers said.
Telecom, which has a substantial weighting in the Top 40 index, closed up 8.0 cents at $7.80, for another year high, having accelerated to a peak of $7.90 during the session.
David Price of First NZ Capital said of the Telecom squeeze, "I think what you're seeing is overseas investment into a market where there is no domestic supply.
"Most institituions are either underweight or at market (weighting), and they're loath to sell any more." He noted that the early index rise would have raised the buying pressure.
